A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete 44-page contents, including equations, figures, tables, proofs, and experimental appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original Monte Carlo experiments on Gaussian approximation errors and attack detection, including a MNIST label-flipping experiment in Section 13.2.1.

after.justification: v4 retains the original simulation results and MNIST attack-detection results, including the numerical outcomes in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The local SGD algorithm, Aggr-GA and Client-GA constructions, weighted multiplier bootstrap, and Algorithm 2 for attack detection retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same federated random-effects simulations, synthetic attack scenarios, and MNIST label-flipping task. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons in Sections 4.3, 12.6, and 12.7 retain Aggr-GA, Client-GA, and the functional-CLT Brownian-motion approximation. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Experimental metrics, step sizes, client counts, synchronization settings, and attack procedures are unchanged. The MNIST experiment retains three-component PCA, five clients, 200 iterations, and an attack at iteration 50.

E4.justification: The heterogeneity, synchronization, network-topology, and time-uniform approximation analyses in Section 12 are retained, as are the attack-detection studies. Removing the heterogeneity corollary does not remove its accompanying empirical analysis.

E5.justification: The reported Monte Carlo repetition counts and bootstrap sample counts are unchanged. Tables 4 and 5 retain the same means and 95% confidence-interval reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4, Tables 1–5, and the two unnumbered ablation tables retain their results. For example, Table 5 reports the same 0.06 false-positive rate and 0.90 label-flipping detection probability in both versions.

T1.justification: v4 corrects Equation (7.1) by subtracting the client gradient at the global optimum, using the client Hessian, and acknowledging a Hessian-Lipschitz condition. It removes v3's auxiliary heterogeneity-dependent Corollary 12.1. The synchronization bound survives unchanged as v4's Corollary 12.1, formerly Corollary 12.2; the main theorems and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about Berry-Esseen bounds, computation-communication trade-offs, time-uniform Gaussian approximations, and bootstrap attack detection.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 newly qualifies the quadratic-remainder argument as requiring Hessian Lipschitz continuity; v3 attributed it solely to Assumptions 7.2 and 7.3. The interpretations of experimental trends, privacy trade-offs, and other limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, simulation specifications, MNIST preprocessing, covariance-estimation instructions, and code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 removes the introductory citations and bibliography entries for Kim et al. (2020), 'Blockchained on-device federated learning,' and Singh et al. (2023), 'Privacy-preserving decentralized federated learning: Algorithms, challenges, and opportunities.' The substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to dates, bibliography metadata, and short appendix passages; the section structure and narrative are retained. v4 introduces an unresolved introductory citation and a dangling 'Corollary ??' reference after Theorem 2.1.

P2.justification: Text reflow shifts some displays, including Table 2 from page 41 to page 40 and Figure 4 upward within page 42. Figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (7.1) and acknowledging the needed Hessian regularity improve mathematical clarity. However, v4 withdraws the explicit heterogeneity bound without explaining whether this corrects an error or sacrifices useful detail, and leaves unresolved citation and corollary references. With the main proofs and empirical evidence unchanged, these mixed effects do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
